answer.text:
The clearest example of something agreed and then never done is obtaining the remaining shelf life data field. In the April 2024 technical due diligence, Tomas Lindholm asked whether remaining shelf life was obtainable and Priya Nair agreed to ask the warehouse team [T02U0132, T02U0133]; Tomas noted it changes the design [T02U0134]. [1] [2] [3]

In May 2024 Priya confirmed she had asked and would chase in August [E11M004]. In August 2024 the answer came back: goods receipt date is captured but not exposed outside the WMS, and getting it would need either an extract nobody owns or a change request, which Priya said she would not raise for something outside the current phase [E11M002]. Tomas logged it as a phase two dependency and closed the thread [E11M001]. [4] [5] [6]

In July 2025 Nadia Haddad asked Priya directly for the field for the fresh ordering configuration [E01M012]. Priya confirmed MHDHB is total shelf life, not remaining, and said she would ask the warehouse team [E01M011]. In late July she said the warehouse team was partly on holiday and she would chase [E01M009]. In September 2025 she said the field was unowned and told Nadia to proceed with an approximation [E01M003]. Nadia had proposed the approximation and built it [E01M005]. [7] [8] [9] [10] [11]

Fresh went live in December 2025 running on the approximation, not the real field [T18U0009]. In June 2026 Marco Rossi told Robert Kahn the twelve-month ROI was missed because fresh depended on a data field identified as a dependency in April 2024 and never obtained [E20M004]. [12] [13]

Who would have needed to notice: Priya Nair owned the chase on the Acme side [E11M004, E01M009]. Ana Duarte tracked the shelf life field mapping in weekly status reports from July 2025 onward [R01M016, R01M015, R01M014] and put it on the escalation agenda [E01M004]. Lena Fischer and Robert Kahn received the monthly steering reports, which flagged the open data dependency with Acme IT [R02M006]. The archive shows Priya chased, Ana escalated, and the workaround was accepted rather than the field obtained. [4] [9] [14] [15] [16] [17] [18]

Limitation: the archive shows the field was never obtained as of the latest records (June 2026). It does not show whether any action after that date resolved it.

citations.quote:
Hi Priya,

For the fresh ordering configuration we need the remaining shelf life at the point of
order, per article per site. Sofia has described where it comes from operationally but
I need the actual field.

Is it MARA-MHDHB, or is there something Acme-specific?

Thanks
citations.title: Shelf life field mapping - fresh export
citations.author: Nadia Haddad

citations.quote:
Hi,

MHDHB is the total shelf life, not remaining. It is populated for part of the range.

Remaining life at order time is not stored anywhere I know of. It would have to be
derived from goods receipt date, and that is in the warehouse system rather than in SAP.

I will ask the warehouse team.
citations.title: Re: Shelf life field mapping - fresh export
citations.author: Priya Nair

citations.quote: Not yet. Half of them are on holiday. I will chase.
citations.title: Re: Shelf life field mapping - fresh export
citations.author: Priya Nair

citations.quote:
It is not impossible, it is unowned, which in practice is the same thing this year.

Proceed with your approximation.
citations.title: Re: Shelf life field mapping - fresh export
citations.author: Priya Nair

citations.quote:
Hi all,

Adding Nadia (Öberg, not Haddad) who did something similar on another account.

Since remaining shelf life is not available, I propose we proceed with an approximation:
total shelf life from MHDHB minus average days-in-warehouse per article group, which we
can derive from stock turn.

It is not exact. For fast movers it will be close. For slow movers it will be wrong in
the direction of assuming the stock is fresher than it is.

If nobody objects I will build it that way so we are not blocked.
citations.title: Re: Shelf life field mapping - fresh export
citations.author: Nadia Haddad

citations.quote: Yes, with the caveat everyone in this room knows. It runs on the approximation. Total shell life minus average days
citations.title: Fresh cutover call
citations.author: Nadia Haddad

citations.quote:
Robert,

Indicative numbers attached. Summary here so you have it in the mail.

Chain wide for the three fresh categories, 340 stores: additional annual licence of
approximately 420 thousand, plus implementation of approximately 260 thousand one off.

On your second point, and this is the honest version.

The twelve month expectation was missed for one reason above all others. The value case
depended on fresh, and fresh depended on a data field that we identified as a dependency
in April 2024 and never obtained. Everything else largely went to plan. We built a
workaround in September 2025 which works acceptably on fast moving articles and poorly on
slow moving ones, and your category manager has been compensating for the difference by
hand ever since.

For the next number to be different, that field has to be available. It is not a RELEX
deliverable and I cannot commit to it on your behalf, which is why I am putting it in
writing rather than in a slide.

If it is not resolved, chain wide will reduce waste by less than the pilot suggests,
because the slow moving articles are a larger share of the tail across 340 stores than
across 25.
